title: Spinal cord disorders
summary: Spinal cord disorders, characterized by A) complete loss of function, B) motor function disorganization in two extremities, or C) marked physical functioning limitation AND in one of four mental functioning areas — in each case persisting for 3 consecutive months after the disorder.

children.criterion: Documented spinal cord disorder (traumatic or non-traumatic, e.g., SCI, myelopathy, transverse myelitis)
Paragraph A (complete loss of function), B (motor function), or C (marked limitation + mental area)
Complete loss of function, as described in 11.00M2, persisting for 3 consecutive months after the disorder (see 11.00M4)

Disorganization of motor function in two extremities (see 11.00D1), resulting in an extreme limitation (see 11.00D2) in the ability to stand up from a seated position, balance while standing or walking, or use the upper extremities, persisting for 3 consecutive months after the disorder (see 11.00M4)
Marked limitation (see 11.00G2) in physical functioning (see 11.00G3a), AND in one of four mental functioning areas, both persisting for 3 consecutive months after the disorder
Marked limitation in ONE of four mental functioning areas
Marked limitation in understanding, remembering, or applying information (see 11.00G3b(i))
Marked limitation in interacting with others (see 11.00G3b(ii))
Marked limitation in concentrating, persisting, or maintaining pace (see 11.00G3b(iii))
Marked limitation in adapting or managing oneself (see 11.00G3b(iv))
Both the physical limitation and the mental limitation persisting for 3 consecutive months after the disorder
